drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 88-year-old female admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.52, creatinine 0.87, hemoglobin 12.8, platelets 307, sodium 141, wbc 6.7; vitals dbp 70-73, heart_rate 78-83, map 88-90, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 124-126, spo2 97-98, temp 36.8-37
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.88, hemoglobin 13, platelets 304, sodium 140, wbc 6.5; vitals dbp 71-74, heart_rate 80-84, map 89-92, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-17, sbp 124-130, spo2 97-98, temp 36.7-37
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 88-year-old female, length of stay 3 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
